newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong demonstrators protest at China plans.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong demonstrators protest at China plans.

text.p: Pro-democracy demonstrators marched through Hong Kong and activists sent balloons into China on Saturday to protest against a new body that will make laws in the territory when China takes it back next year.

"We are here today to protest against the setting up of the illegal body, the provisional legislature," independent lawmaker Emily Lau told demonstrators in a square beside the chambers of the current Legislative Council.
"We want the Chinese government to respect our wishes and allow us to have democracy," she said.

As Lau spoke and demonstrators chanted "Oppose the provisional legislature", votes cast by 400 carefully chosen electors were tallied across the border in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for the 60 people who will make up Hong Kong's post-handover legislature.
China plans to install the provisional chamber, which Saturday's vote showed will include 33 incumbent lawmakers, when it takes back the territory from Britain at midnight on June 30.
The Legislative Council that was elected by more than one million Hong Kong voters last year will be disbanded.

"Today we will have two legislatures in one territory," Democratic Party legislator Andrew Cheng told the demonstrators, who were nearly outnumbered by onlookers and journalists. "This is a constitutional crisis."
Carrying placards and banners, the demonstrators marched through central Hong Kong chanting slogans and handing out leaflets as police diverted Saturday afternoon traffic.
The number of marchers grew to about 200 as they moved along busy Queen's Road to the office of China's Xinhua news agency, Beijing's de facto embassy in the territory.
One Hong Kong resident watching from a footbridge said he did not support the demonstrators.
"I feel they will affect Hong Kong's economic stability," he said. "They don't understand the true Hong Kong heart."
But another observer said it was important the marchers made their opinions known.
"I still want Hong Kong to have more democracy and to have a legislature elected by all the people," he said.

Outside the Xinhua building, the demonstrators chanted slogans behind crowd-control barriers before a small group, including Lau and several other legislators, moved to the front steps. They gave short speeches and affixed a petition to the metal grille covering the doors.

The police presence along the march route and outside the Xinhua offices was relatively light, although there were about 150 officers and several police vans lined up in the laneway behind the building.

Earlier in the day, Cheng and other members of the United Front Against the Provisional Legislature drove into a restricted area at the Lok Ma Chau border post and sent 50 helium-filled balloons attached to a banner urging people to "oppose the provisional legislature" drifting into China.
Police allowed the protest to take place but then asked the group to leave the area.
Cheng said members released the balloons because China would not let them travel over the border to Shenzhen.
"We cannot go into the Shenzhen area to protest but our balloons -- our spirit of protest -- will continue to fight against such an anti-democratic body," Cheng said.
